winner.text: Increase same-user negative sampling from one to four negatives per eligible positive in the pairwise logistic objective.
winner.rationale: Experiment 3 improved both official components over the pointwise parent (GAUC 0.67060 versus 0.66891; nDCG@5 0.53753 versus 0.53696), so increasing negative coverage is a focused way to strengthen the already validated ordering signal. The largest remaining nDCG weakness is on tab 0 and tab 6, where more within-user alternatives may improve discrimination.
winner.exact_ablation: Change only the pair constructor so each eligible positive training row samples K=4 same-user negative rows uniformly without replacement when possible, instead of K=1; retain the additive five-field scorer, pairwise logistic loss, optimizer, learning rate, regularization, epoch budget, and stopping rule.

expected_effect.GAUC: Increase by 0.0005 to 0.0025 because each positive receives broader same-user negative comparisons.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Increase by 0.0005 to 0.0030 if additional comparisons correct top-five inversions; the effect may be concentrated in low-performing tabs.

selection_rationale: c01 is the best next scarce experiment because it is the consultant's top-ranked option (utility 0.86) and directly extends the only measured, validated improvement: experiment 3 raised primary from 0.60293485 to 0.60406537, with both GAUC (0.67060 vs 0.66891) and nDCG@5 (0.53753 vs 0.53696) improving. Increasing from one to four same-user negatives is a tightly scoped, low-leakage modification that should reduce sampling variance and strengthen the already successful ordering signal without introducing new features, architecture, or loss complexity. Its expected primary gain of 0.0015 is among the highest, confidence is relatively strong (6), and its medium runtime cost is materially safer than exhaustive negatives, hard mining, or listwise/LambdaRank alternatives.
